title: Agent Supply Chain Security
summary: Track and verify the origin, integrity, permissions, and release compatibility of models, prompts, tools, connectors, and agent dependencies.
overview: An agent's supply chain extends beyond application packages. Behavior depends on model artifacts or hosted versions, prompt bundles, tool schemas, connector binaries, retrieval corpora, policy files, and runtime images. A change to any of these can alter the actions the system takes even when application code is unchanged.

Build a release manifest that identifies every behavior-relevant dependency and its approved provenance. Verify artifacts before execution and separate content acquisition from authority to enable capabilities. Signed provenance can show where an artifact came from and how it was built; it does not prove the artifact is safe, correct, or appropriate for the workflow.

production.poc: A proof of concept should inventory external packages, models, prompts, and tools and avoid executing downloaded components with broad host credentials.
production.production: Production requires pinned artifacts, integrity verification, reviewed capability changes, dependency scanning, provenance records, and release evaluation of the complete agent bundle.
production.scale: Enterprise scale adds trusted build identities, private registries, transitive dependency review, emergency revocation, reproducible release manifests, and ownership across connector and model providers.

components.name: Dependency and capability inventory
components.role: Lists packages, models, prompts, corpora, tools, and the permissions each component can exercise.

components.name: Trusted build pipeline
components.role: Produces immutable artifacts and provenance tied to controlled source and build identities.

components.name: Artifact registry
components.role: Stores approved versions, digests, attestations, ownership, and revocation status.

components.name: Admission verifier
components.role: Checks integrity, provenance policy, compatibility, and requested capabilities before enabling a release.

components.name: Runtime monitor and rollback controller
components.role: Detects unexpected capability or artifact changes and returns to an approved compatible release when necessary.

flow.title: Inventory behavior inputs
flow.description: Enumerate executable dependencies and non-code artifacts that influence tool selection, retrieval, policy, or model behavior.

flow.title: Build and attest
flow.description: Produce controlled artifacts and provenance identifying source, build process, and immutable output digests.

flow.title: Review capability changes
flow.description: Compare requested permissions and tool schemas with the previous release; route material expansion to the responsible owner.

flow.title: Verify before activation
flow.description: Check digests, trusted provenance, revocation status, compatibility, and evaluation evidence for the entire release bundle.

flow.title: Run with constrained authority
flow.description: Grant only approved capabilities and observe actual tool use so a trusted artifact cannot silently acquire broader permissions.

flow.title: Revoke and recover
flow.description: Disable compromised versions, identify affected workflows through manifests, and roll back only to a compatible approved bundle.

useCase.title: Connector release integrity
useCase.situation: Illustrative architecture: A platform team upgrades a document connector used by several customer-facing assistants.
useCase.problem: The new package may contain an unexpected dependency or advertise a write capability that the old release did not expose.
useCase.requirement: Verify the deployed artifact and explicitly review any permission expansion before customer workflows can use it.
useCase.architecture: A release manifest pins connector digest, tool schema, prompt bundle, and policy version; admission verifies provenance and evaluation results before enabling the connector.
useCase.failure: The runtime discovers a tool schema that differs from the approved manifest; the connector is quarantined until the owner reviews the change.
useCase.impact: Measure manifest coverage, verified artifact rate, unreviewed capability changes, revocation propagation time, and recovery success rather than equating signatures with security.

tradeoffs.benefit: Make releases reconstructable and unexpected changes visible.
tradeoffs.cost: Require deliberate updates and emergency patch workflows.

tradeoffs.benefit: Establishes artifact origin and build identity.
tradeoffs.cost: Does not replace vulnerability analysis or behavioral evaluation.

tradeoffs.benefit: Capture non-code changes that affect agent behavior.
tradeoffs.cost: Increase coordination across model, content, connector, and platform owners.

failures.scenario: A package registry serves a different artifact under a familiar version label.
failures.detection: Digest verification fails against the approved release manifest.
failures.recovery: Block deployment, quarantine the artifact, and investigate the registry or build path.

failures.scenario: A trusted connector update expands its tool permissions silently.
failures.detection: Capability diff or runtime schema checks detect an unapproved operation.
failures.recovery: Disable the new capability and require owner review and regression evidence before activation.

mistakes.mistake: Auditing application packages while ignoring prompts and tool schemas.
mistakes.fix: Inventory all behavior-relevant artifacts and their release ownership.

mistakes.mistake: Treating a valid signature as proof of safe behavior.
mistakes.fix: Combine provenance with scanning, permission review, isolation, and workflow evaluation.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling back one component without checking compatibility.
mistakes.fix: Restore a tested bundle whose models, prompts, tools, and policy versions work together.

whenToUse: Agents depend on third-party tools, connectors, executable plugins, or downloaded model artifacts.
Several teams independently update components that affect agent behavior.
A platform needs to identify and revoke every workflow using a compromised dependency.
whenNotToUse: A component has no executable or behavior-changing role in the agent workflow.
The proposed verification process cannot identify an accountable artifact owner or trusted build source.
Provenance checks would be used as a substitute for runtime authorization and isolation.
checklist: Inventory code and non-code dependencies that affect agent behavior.
Pin immutable artifact digests and maintain a complete release manifest.
Verify provenance against trusted build identities before activation.
Review tool schema and permission changes independently of package version changes.
Evaluate the complete model, prompt, tool, corpus, and policy bundle.
Constrain runtime capabilities even for approved signed artifacts.
Test revocation propagation and compatible rollback across affected workflows.
